Standalone DP checked 40,466 interior instances and 977 successor instances across 977 pairs; 20 additional direct base-order calculations concur.

originality.rationale: Theorem 1 of the 2022 progression paper explicitly terminates at p=floor(a/2); the new domain extends from p=floor(a/2)+2 through a+d and proves the first strict break. The 2023 three-variable theorem requires an inapplicable divisor relation. The closest public full-text three-phase result treats d=1 only, and a general eventual theorem does not imply this uniform intermediate parameter statement. Full texts/primary theorems were inspected, semantic published-finding corpus searches and semantically related published records were compared by their actual ranges. An implicit equivalence in broader literature remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: A more general restricted-partition closed formula could implicitly specialize to this sharp two-parameter phase without naming the same interval.
Unindexed or inaccessible numerical-semigroup tables, especially higher-p Apéry order statistics, might contain equivalent results.
The current review is not an independent mathematical audit.

value.rationale: The same triple-progression p-Frobenius problem has established initial-phase formulas only up to floor(a/2). The finding supplies a full new linearly long interval in the representation threshold for a two-parameter infinite family and its mathematically meaningful sharp first breakpoint with deficit a-2d. The exact phase is a natural representation-threshold invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice, and may inform higher-level p-Apéry classification.
